title: Functoriality of the etale torsor classification of H1
statement: Use, for abelian sheaves on small etale sites, the canonical bijection $H^1(T_{\mathrm{Et}},G)\cong\{\text{isomorphism classes of }G\text{-torsors}\}$ of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] (torsors as in [def-sc-gm-torsor]). (1) Let $u:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and $u^*:H^1(X_{\mathrm{Et}},G)\to H^1(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},u^{-1}G)$ the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. For a $G$-torsor $T$, the inverse image $u^{-1}T$ of the sheaf of sets $T$ (the sheafified presheaf inverse image, as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]) is a $u^{-1}G$-torsor, and $u^*$ sends the class of $T$ to the class of $u^{-1}T$. (2) Let $S$ be a scheme and $\varphi:G\to G'$ a morphism of abelian sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, with $H^1(\varphi):H^1(S_{\mathrm{Et}},G)\to H^1(S_{\mathrm{Et}},G')$ the induced map of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. Then $H^1(\varphi)$ sends the class of a $G$-torsor $T$ to the class of the $G'$-torsor $T\wedge^GG'$, the sheafification of $(T\times G')/G$ with $g\cdot(t,g')=(g\cdot t,\varphi(g)^{-1}g')$ and $G'$ acting on the second factor.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ (torsors and H^1) together with functoriality of the extension E_T: u^{-1}E_T=E_{u^{-1}T} and the pushout of E_T along phi is E_{T wedge G'}; compare the Zariski version lem-sc-torsor-h1-functoriality (1)

proof.text: For a G-torsor T, the canonical bijection of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] is represented by the short exact sequence $0\to G\to E_T\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ and sends [T] to the connecting image of 1. Pulling this sequence back along u and using [lem-sc-etale-torsor-inverse-image-extension] identifies the pulled-back extension with E_{u^{-1}T}, whose fibre over 1 is u^{-1}T.

source.place: Lemma 03AJ, construction by the extension E_T and functoriality under inverse image

proof.text: By [lem-sc-etale-torsor-inverse-image-extension], $0\to u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}E_T\to\mathbf Z_Y\to0$ is the inverse image of $0\to G\to E_T\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ and is the extension $E_{u^{-1}T}$. Clause 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] (the pullback maps $u^*$ commute with the connecting maps, $u^*\circ\delta^0_X=\delta^0_Y\circ u^*$) gives $u^*(\delta_{E_T}(1))=\delta_{E_{u^{-1}T}}(u^*1)$, and $u^*1=1$ in $H^0(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z_Y)$ since in degree zero $u^*$ is pullback of global sections [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero]. By the representative description in [lem-sc-torsor-h1], $\delta_{E_T}(1)=[T]$ and $\delta_{E_{u^{-1}T}}(1)=[u^{-1}T]$, proving clause (1).

source.place: Lemma 03AJ, functoriality of the boundary class under inverse image

proof.text: For a morphism $\varphi:G\to G'$ on S, represent [T] by the extension E_T from [lem-sc-torsor-h1]. By [lem-sc-etale-torsor-pushout-extension], its pushout along $\varphi$ is a short exact sequence with fibre T wedge^G G'.

source.place: Lemma 03AJ, pushout of E_T along phi and identification of its fibre

proof.text: The canonical map $E_T\to E_T\wedge^GG'$ together with $\varphi$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf Z_S}$ is a morphism from $0\to G\to E_T\to\mathbf Z_S\to0$ to the pushout sequence of [lem-sc-etale-torsor-pushout-extension]. Etale cohomology $H^q(S_{\mathrm{Et}},-)$ is the right derived functor of the left exact functor $\Gamma(S,-)$ on $\Ab(S_{\mathrm{Et}})$ (which has enough injectives), so by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] it is a $\delta$-functor, whose connecting maps commute with morphisms of short exact sequences: $H^1(\varphi)(\delta_{E_T}(1))=\delta_{E_T\wedge^GG'}(\mathrm{id}(1))=\delta_{E_T\wedge^GG'}(1)$, with $H^1(\varphi)$ the map of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. The representative description of [lem-sc-torsor-h1], applied to the $G'$-torsor $T\wedge^GG'$ (the fibre over $1$ of the pushout sequence), therefore identifies $H^1(\varphi)([T])$ with $[T\wedge^GG']$, proving clause (2).
